method_card.title: Forces, Work Done and Elasticity
method_card.content: Four equations that are easy to mix up. Weight \(W = mg\) is a force in newtons, not a mass. Work done \(W = Fd\) needs the distance moved along the force (joules). Hooke's law \(F = ke\) links spring force to extension, with e in metres. Elastic PE \(E = \tfrac{1}{2}ke^2\) squares the extension, so doubling it quadruples the energy. Check whether your board gives you these equations or expects them from memory. The usual slips are extension in cm not m, and forgetting to square e.

steps: Two equations in a row: work out the first quantity, then use it in the second.
For a launch, elastic energy becomes kinetic energy: ½ke² = ½mv², then solve for v.
Ignore distractor numbers; use only the force or energy the question actually needs.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange \(E = \tfrac{1}{2} k e^2\) to \(k = 2E \div e^2\). Here E = 2 J and e = 0.10 m.

guided_steps.hint: Two times the stored energy.
0.1 times 0.1.
The 4 on top, e squared on the bottom.

guided_steps.done: Back to 2 J stored, so k = 400 N/m is right.

Rearrange E = ½ke² for k: k = 2E ÷ e² = (2 × 2) ÷ 0.10² = 4 ÷ 0.01 = 400 N/m.

guided_steps.say: Elastic PE first: \(E = \tfrac{1}{2} k e^2\), with k = 400 N/m and e = 0.30 m.

guided_steps.hint: 0.3 times 0.3.
Half of 400 is 200, then times 0.09.

guided_steps.say: All 18 J becomes kinetic energy, so \(\tfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = 18\) with m = 0.05 kg.

Square the draw distance in the elastic PE: E = ½ × 400 × 0.30² = 18 J, then v = √(2 × 18 ÷ 0.05) = 26.83 m/s.

guided_steps.pre: Put the force on top: e = 5 ÷
